specification_compliance: I1/I2/I3/I5: addons/media_import/frontend/players/YouTubeEmbed.tsx:484 computes gesturesInteractive = !adActive && (!ended || fullscreen.isFullscreen), and line 563 passes it to MediaControls. GestureOverlay.tsx:46 turns it into pointerEvents auto/none. With no ad the overlay is auto during playback, auto at ENDED in fullscreen and none at ENDED in the page. During an ad it is always none.

I4: useFullscreen.ts:125 sets pseudoOpen = phase === 'on', and line 205 sets isFullscreen = nativeActive || pseudoOpen, while isPseudo (pseudoActive) also covers 'closing'. isFullscreen therefore turns false when the carry back starts and the frame is still pinned. ended is React state and does not change, so gesturesInteractive goes to false on that same render without a new player state.
I6: YouTubeEmbed.tsx:339-349 calls notifyEnded and onEnded once per ENDED state change unless isInterrupted(). This path does not depend on fullscreen and the change did not touch it.
I7: MediaControlsContainer.tsx:96/292/380/406 receives interactive. At ENDED in fullscreen it gets the same value it gets during a pause (true), and at ENDED in the page it gets false.
potential_unspecified_behavior: While pseudo fullscreen is opening (phase 'opening'), isFullscreen is still false, so at ENDED the overlay stays none until the pin takes effect. This matches I4, which ties the change to isFullscreen.
regression_risks: At ENDED in fullscreen, backendOwnsFrame (MediaControlsContainer.tsx:406, !interactive) is now false, where it used to be true. Gestures, the scrim and tap/click handling now behave as they do during a pause, which is what I7 asks for, but YouTube's own end-screen tiles in fullscreen are covered by the overlay.
